chunks: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'The house in which the Quran is recited and wherein God, Mighty and Majestic, is remembered, its blessing will be abundant, the angels will attend it, and the devils will forsake it, and it will shine for the inhabitants of the sky just as the stars shine for the inhabitants of the earth. And indeed the house in which the Quran is not recited and God, Mighty and Majestic, is not remembered, its blessing will be scarce, the angels will forsake it, and the devils will attend it.'

key_terms.البركة: Divine blessing and abundance — understood as both material prosperity and spiritual grace
key_terms.البيت: The household — the physical and spiritual domain of family life and practice
key_terms.الشياطين: Satans/Devils — forces of spiritual corruption that fill the vacuum left by absence of dhikr
key_terms.الكواكب: Stars/planets — used here as a metaphor for the luminous quality of a house of dhikr
key_terms.الملائكة: Angels — spiritual beings who attend to spaces of remembrance and worship

ai.seo_question: What happens spiritually to a house where the Quran is recited regularly?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) draws a vivid contrast between two types of households: those filled with Quranic recitation and remembrance of God, and those devoid of it. The spiritually active household is described as a beacon of divine blessing that literally radiates light visible to the angels in the heavens, while the neglectful household becomes a dwelling place of demonic presence. This teaching was given to early Muslim communities for whom the home was the primary arena of religious practice, emphasizing that spiritual discipline must be rooted in the family environment.
